title: Data Plane Observability Governance: Adaptive PII Masking & Access Trails
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive, low-latency observability dataplane that enforces per-tenant PII governance across traces, metrics annotation, and log pipelines while preserving correlation for debugging. This ticket covers: 1) tracing hooks and metadata tagging that propagate redaction context; 2) an inline pipeline stage that applies adaptive masking (allowlist/denylist/tokenization) based on request context and tenant policy; 3) separation of raw/derived telemetry streams and TTL-driven retention; 4) immutable access trails for who queried telemetry and why; and 5) RBAC integration so only authorized service accounts or users can retrieve PII-sensitive views. We must balance performance (token throughput/latency) with compliance needs (GDPR/SOC2).
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hook added: traces carry a redaction-context header that indicates tenant policy and sampling decision and is propagated across services
Pipeline stage implemented: telemetry ingestion pipeline supports a configurable adaptive masker with 3 modes (scrub, pseudonymize, allow) applied per-tenant
Retention: telemetry streams can be routed into two tiered stores (short-term high-cardinality, long-term scrubbed) and TTLs configurable per-tenant
Access logging: all reads of PII-sensitive telemetry generate immutable audit events with user/service, query, timestamp, and justification
RBAC: Console/API honors new telemetry access roles and denies PII views to non-authorized principals
Performance: added masking step increases median ingest latency by < 8ms at 95th percentile under standard load (validated in canary)
E2E tests and a runbook for responding to suspected unintended exposure are added and reviewed
Security review completed and KMS integration for pseudonymization secrets approved
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2025-03-03: Use deterministic pseudonymization (HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-scoped key in KMS) for correlating entities across runs without retaining raw values
Decision 2025-03-05: Implement adaptive masking in the ingestion datapath (fast-path native C++ stage) instead of post-processing to simplify retention guarantees
Decision 2025-03-07: Split telemetry into two Kafka topics: telemetry.raw (short-lived, encrypted, access-restricted) and telemetry.scrubbed (longer TTL, readable by broader teams)
Trade-off: Additional CPU for masking vs. cost of retaining raw telemetry; chose masking in-path to reduce long-term storage and simplify compliance
Policy model: tenant policy defined by allowlist/denylist for field patterns, plus override roles for SRE/forensics with just-in-time approval
implementation_plan: Week 1: Add redaction-context header to trace instrumentation (go, python, node) and update SDKs; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482

Week 2: Build adaptive masking stage in ingestion service (C++), expose policy API in governance service; design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Observability+Data+Plane+Governance
Week 3: Wire KMS HMAC keys for pseudonymization; add unit tests and performance benchmarks
Week 4: Deploy canary for a single mid-size tenant behind an opt-in flag; collect latency/throughput metrics and audit logs
Week 5: Dashboarding: add PII exposure and access-log dashboards in Console; update latency/error dashboards to include masking SLO impact
Week 6: Rollout to GA with migration playbook and runbook for incident response
